summary: An outline item whose /A is a go-to action stating /SD resolves to /D's page. outline::destination reads the action's /D alone (Destination::read(document, action.get("D")?)), while a link's go-to, the catalog's /OpenAction and a named destination's dictionary form all go through Destination::of_go_to / preferring_structure, which takes /SD first. Item::destination is what Outline::section_at maps pages back to items with, so the section a page is announced under (Event::PageChanged's section, the title bar) is the /D page's; activating the item is not affected, because interact::activate_object reads /A through action::read.
source: ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.2, Table 202, SD: "If present, the structure destination should take precedence over destination in the D entry." §12.3.3, Table 151, A: "The action that shall be performed when this item is activated".

summary: A remote go-to's structure destination decides only the page. remote_go_to keeps /SD's first element (the element's ID) and drops the rest of the array, and interact's place_remote applies /D's view only where /D named the same page (ADR 2964), so /SD [(id) /XYZ 40 700 2] shows the element's page at whatever view was current. And where the element is found but identifies no page, RemoteGoTo::page_in falls through to /D, where §12.3.2.3 (and the local reading, Destination::resolve) take the first page.
source: ISO 32000-2 §12.3.2.3: "The structure element shall be used to identify the page to which the content belongs and, using that page, the structure destination shall behave identically to a destination." and "In the case where no page content is identified, then the page reference shall be assumed to be the first page in the document." §12.6.4.3, Table 203, SD: "If present, the structure destination should take precedence over destination in the D entry."

summary: A /Next chain moves the view once. interact::resolve keeps the first page any request names (Jump::take is a no-op once a page is set, Request::Page uses `or_else`) and computes Named NextPage/PrevPage from the page the chain started on, so NextPage followed by NextPage advances one page, a go-to to page 2 followed by NextPage stays on page 2, and a go-to followed by a second go-to shows the first. The comment beside it says a chain that jumps twice "has shown the second page either way" (D02).
source: ISO 32000-2 §12.6.2, Table 196, Next: "The value is either a single action dictionary or an array of action dictionaries that shall be performed in order"; §12.6.4.12, Table 215: NextPage "Go to the next page of the document."
